facts.text: **Glenn Maxwell** retired from international cricket: 7 Tests, 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is.
facts.plain: Glenn Maxwell retired from international cricket: 7 Tests, 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is.

facts.text: Previous youngest champion: **Sebastian Vettel** (23 years 134 days, 2010). Antonelli is the first Italian champion since **Alberto Ascari (1953)**.
facts.plain: Previous youngest champion: Sebastian Vettel (23 years 134 days, 2010). Antonelli is the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari (1953).

facts.text: **Kimi Antonelli** (Mercedes, Italy) became the youngest F1 champion at **20 years 68 days**, finishing 3rd in the Mexico City GP won by Max Verstappen.
facts.plain: Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes, Italy) became the youngest F1 champion at 20 years 68 days, finishing 3rd in the Mexico City GP won by Max Verstappen.

facts.text: **Manav Thakkar** won his first international singles title at **WTT Feeder Chennai**, beating England's Samuel Walker in the final; **Sutirtha Mukherjee** was runner-up in women's singles to Korea's Yoo Yerin.
facts.plain: Manav Thakkar won his first international singles title at WTT Feeder Chennai, beating England's Samuel Walker in the final; Sutirtha Mukherjee was runner-up in women's singles to Korea's Yoo Yerin.

facts.text: **Marc Marquez** moved to the brink of an eighth MotoGP world title after winning the Malaysian GP, extending his points lead to 399 (second-placed brother Alex Marquez on 355) with three race weekends left.
facts.plain: Marc Marquez moved to the brink of an eighth MotoGP world title after winning the Malaysian GP, extending his points lead to 399 (second-placed brother Alex Marquez on 355) with three race weekends left.

facts.text: India's men's and women's kabaddi teams won the titles at the inaugural **Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship** in Ahmedabad; the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 and the women beat Uganda 35-15.
facts.plain: India's men's and women's kabaddi teams won the titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad; the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 and the women beat Uganda 35-15.

facts.text: **Carlos Alcaraz** beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open — his fourth title of the year and 28th overall.
facts.plain: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open — his fourth title of the year and 28th overall.

facts.text: New Zealand won the fifth T20I by seven wickets (Tim Seifert 93*), but **India won the series 3-2** after taking the first three games — captain **Shreyas Iyer's** first series win in a **SENA** country.
facts.plain: New Zealand won the fifth T20I by seven wickets (Tim Seifert 93*), but India won the series 3-2 after taking the first three games — captain Shreyas Iyer's first series win in a SENA country.

facts.text: New Zealand's **Glenn Phillips** became the highest run-scorer in a bilateral T20I series with 341 runs against India in five matches, surpassing England's Phil Salt's 331 (2023).
facts.plain: New Zealand's Glenn Phillips became the highest run-scorer in a bilateral T20I series with 341 runs against India in five matches, surpassing England's Phil Salt's 331 (2023).

facts.text: **P.V. Sindhu** and **Lakshya Sen** won the women's and men's singles titles at the Hylo Open Super 500 (Saarbrucken, Germany) with straight-games final wins — Sindhu's title adds to her earlier Japan Open win this year, and Lakshya ended a title drought.
facts.plain: P.V. Sindhu and Lakshya Sen won the women's and men's singles titles at the Hylo Open Super 500 (Saarbrucken, Germany) with straight-games final wins — Sindhu's title adds to her earlier Japan Open win this year, and Lakshya ended a title drought.

facts.text: Indian Navy beat Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) 5-4 in a penalty shootout to win the **97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup** hockey title in Chennai.
facts.plain: Indian Navy beat Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) 5-4 in a penalty shootout to win the 97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup hockey title in Chennai.

facts.text: Teen paddler **Swara Karmarkar** (16, Nashik; world No. 947) reached the WTT Feeder Chennai semis as a qualifier; Bengaluru's **Chiranth Vishwanath** (Petronas TVS) won the Super Sport 301-400cc race in the **MRF Indian National Racing Championship** (2W).
facts.plain: Teen paddler Swara Karmarkar (16, Nashik; world No. 947) reached the WTT Feeder Chennai semis as a qualifier; Bengaluru's Chiranth Vishwanath (Petronas TVS) won the Super Sport 301-400cc race in the MRF Indian National Racing Championship (2W).

facts.text: Third **WTA 250 Chennai Open** (SDAT Stadium): wild cards to **Vaishnavi Adkar** (India No. 1, WTA 334), Maaya Rajeshwaran and Sahaja Yamalapalli; defending champion **Janice Tjen** (Indonesia); TNTA president **Vijay Amritraj**.
facts.plain: Third WTA 250 Chennai Open (SDAT Stadium): wild cards to Vaishnavi Adkar (India No. 1, WTA 334), Maaya Rajeshwaran and Sahaja Yamalapalli; defending champion Janice Tjen (Indonesia); TNTA president Vijay Amritraj.

facts.text: **Kolkata** hosts the **AFC Women's Champions League** group (Kishore Bharati Stadium): Indian Women's League champion **East Bengal** vs Ho Chi Minh City, Korea's Hwacheon KSPO and DPR Korea's April 25 SC.
facts.plain: Kolkata hosts the AFC Women's Champions League group (Kishore Bharati Stadium): Indian Women's League champion East Bengal vs Ho Chi Minh City, Korea's Hwacheon KSPO and DPR Korea's April 25 SC.

facts.text: Men's **Asian Champions Trophy** (Jalandhar; started **2011**): India is ranked **8th**, the only Asian team in the top 10; coach **Craig Fulton**. India beat Malaysia **5-1** in the **Asian Games** final to qualify for the **LA 2028 Olympics**.
facts.plain: Men's Asian Champions Trophy (Jalandhar; started 2011): India is ranked 8th, the only Asian team in the top 10; coach Craig Fulton. India beat Malaysia 5-1 in the Asian Games final to qualify for the LA 2028 Olympics.

facts.text: **Manisha Bhanwala** (29, Siwaha, **Jind**) said she chose non-Olympic **59kg** for the Worlds; she joins **Sushil Kumar** (2010) as an Indian world champion and won the final 8-6 over USA's Abigail Nette. Coach: **Virender Dahiya**. Indian men's freestyle wrestlers won no medal.
facts.plain: Manisha Bhanwala (29, Siwaha, Jind) said she chose non-Olympic 59kg for the Worlds; she joins Sushil Kumar (2010) as an Indian world champion and won the final 8-6 over USA's Abigail Nette. Coach: Virender Dahiya. Indian men's freestyle wrestlers won no medal.

facts.text: **West Indies** beat Bangladesh by 8 wickets in the 1st Test at **Mirpur** (Roston Chase 5/36); **Pakistan** beat Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final in **Lahore** (**Fakhar Zaman** 127). Pacer **Auqib Nabi** joined India's ODI squad for the NZ series (1st ODI at **Eden Park**, Auckland).
facts.plain: West Indies beat Bangladesh by 8 wickets in the 1st Test at Mirpur (Roston Chase 5/36); Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final in Lahore (Fakhar Zaman 127). Pacer Auqib Nabi joined India's ODI squad for the NZ series (1st ODI at Eden Park, Auckland).

facts.text: **Simon Harmer** (6/16; first 10-wicket match haul) bowled out Australia for **111** at **Newlands** as **South Africa** (captain **Temba Bavuma**) won the series **2-1** and became **No. 1 in the ICC Test rankings**; Player of the Series: **Marco Jansen**.
facts.plain: Simon Harmer (6/16; first 10-wicket match haul) bowled out Australia for 111 at Newlands as South Africa (captain Temba Bavuma) won the series 2-1 and became No. 1 in the ICC Test rankings; Player of the Series: Marco Jansen.
keys: No. 1 in the ICC Test rankings

facts.plain: Kagiso Rabada became the fastest to 350 Test wickets by balls (13,808), ahead of Dale Steyn (14,719) and Waqar Younis (14,905).

facts.text: Dakar 2026 is the first Olympic event of any kind held in **Africa**; the Youth Olympic Games began in **2010** (Singapore).
facts.plain: Dakar 2026 is the first Olympic event of any kind held in Africa; the Youth Olympic Games began in 2010 (Singapore).

facts.text: **Alexander Zverev** (Germany, 29) will become **world No. 1** for the first time, replacing **Jannik Sinner** — the 30th different men's No. 1 and the oldest first-timer since **John Newcombe (1974)**. ATP rankings began in **1973**.

facts.text: Indian women's best-ever Worlds: gold (Manisha Bhanwala, 59kg), silver (**Neelam Sirohi** 50kg, **Kajal Dhochak** 76kg), bronze (**Tanu Sharma** 72kg); India finished 4th in the women's section.

facts.text: **Manisha Bhanwala** (Haryana) won **59kg gold** at the **World Wrestling Championships** in **Astana**, beating USA's Abigail Nette 8-6 — the **first Indian woman** to win a world title and India's second world champion after **Sushil Kumar** (66kg, Moscow 2010).
facts.plain: Manisha Bhanwala (Haryana) won 59kg gold at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, beating USA's Abigail Nette 8-6 — the first Indian woman to win a world title and India's second world champion after Sushil Kumar (66kg, Moscow 2010).

facts.text: **31 Oct 1976**: India played its **first women's Test**, against West Indies at the **M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru**; leg-spinner **Shubhangi Kulkarni** took 5/48. India's first women's Test win came in the fourth Test at **Patna**. India has played only 42 more women's Tests since.
facts.plain: 31 Oct 1976: India played its first women's Test, against West Indies at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru; leg-spinner Shubhangi Kulkarni took 5/48. India's first women's Test win came in the fourth Test at Patna. India has played only 42 more women's Tests since.
